Time dependent transmission models require a choice for the infectivity profile $f$, defined as the instantaneous rate of secondary infection caused by a reference infector.
An infectivity profile is thus a function of the time from infection $t_{i}$ to transmission at time $t$, the "generation time" $t - t_{i}$. The profile can also depend on other infector covariates.

In certain applications a profile has to be expressed as a function of the time from symptoms onset $t_{i}^\mathrm{ons}$ to transmission.
In such cases, the profile will be a function of the generation time and of the incubation period $\tau_{i}^\mathrm{inc}$ of the infector, remembering that $t_{i} + \tau_{i}^\mathrm{inc} = t_{i}^\mathrm{ons}$.

Infectivity profiles in housepi depend on covariates of the infector only, not of the infectee.
The "serial time" (the time between symptom onsets of infector and infectee) therefore cannot be the argument of a profile.

In short, assuming $i$ the infector and $k$ the infectee, the time intervals supported by the infectivity profiles in housepi are

<div style="display: flex; justify-content: center;">
<div style="white-space: nowrap;">

| Time Interval |  | Profile | Support |
|---------------|--|---------|:-------:|
| Generation | $t_{k} - t_{i}$ | $f(t_{k} - t_{i})$ | <span style="color: green;">&check;</span> |
| Onset to Transmission | $t_{k} - t_{i}^\mathrm{ons}$ | $f(t_{k} - t_{i}\vert \tau_{i}^\mathrm{inc})$ | <span style="color: green;">&check;</span> |
| Serial | $t_{k}^\mathrm{ons} - t_{i}^\mathrm{ons}$ | $f(t_{k} - t_{i}\vert \tau_{i}^\mathrm{inc}, \tau_{k}^\mathrm{inc})$ | <span style="color: red;">&cross;</span> |

</div>
</div>

According to this scheme, infectivity profile definitions can be of two kinds:

* **Generic**: if all individuals in the study share the same profile;
* **Latent**: if the profile depends on individual covariates.

A model whose transmission is driven by a profile refuses to run until one is defined.
Models shipping a suggested profile expose it through `import = "template"`.

Whatever the profile, it must give no infectivity at generation time 0: nobody transmits at the instant of being infected.
A profile that does is refused, and the error points at the two ways of excluding the origin: truncating the profile with `min`, or shifting it with `loc`.
Distributions such as `exponential` or `uniform` are positive at 0 and need one of the two.
Distributions authored as infectivity profiles, like `ferretti20`, are taken as they are written.

For example, consider the model "case-ascertained" introduced in [Get started](housepi.html).
Its template is a generic profile in continuous time, a gamma distribution parametrized with `mean` and `sd` (see `?template_case_ascertained`):

```{r}
#| label: load-continuous-profile
library(housepi)
set_housepi_theme(colour_strips = TRUE)
set.seed(42)

hhcontinuous <- sarscov2_2021_icofs |>
  new_housepi_model("case-ascertained") |>
  add_infectivity_profile(import = "template")
# extract current loaded profile definitions
defs <- get_infectivity_profiles(hhcontinuous)
# display definitions
defs
# display function arguments
defs$func_args
```

Here we read the definition of the model with `get_infectivity_profiles()`.
We can explore the infectivity profiles by calling `browse_infectivity_profiles`.
This generates an object holding the infectivity profile definitions to be used to compute instantaneous and cumulative values of the profile.

```{r}
#| label: plot-continuous-profile
#| fig-alt: >
#|  Instantaneous infectivity profile as a function of the generation time in black.
#|  On a second axis in orange, the corresponding cumulative infectivity profile.
profile <- browse_infectivity_profiles(defs$func, defs$func_args)

library(ggplot2)

# function to plot a demonstration of both instantaneous and cumulative profiles
plot_profile_demo <- function(profile,
                              color_inst = "black",
                              color_cumul = "coral") {
  infec <- dplyr::tibble(gentime = seq(0, 100, 0.05),
                         inst = profile$inst(gentime),
                         cumul = profile$cumul(gentime))
  # coefficient to re-scale the cumulative
  rescale <- max(infec$cumul) / max(infec$inst)

  ggplot(infec, aes(x = gentime)) +
    # plot cumulative profile
    theme(axis.ticks.y.right = element_line(color = color_cumul),
          axis.text.y.right = element_text(color = color_cumul),
          axis.title.y.right = element_text(color = color_cumul)) +
    geom_line(aes(y = cumul / rescale), color = color_cumul) +
    # plot instantaneous
    geom_line(aes(y = inst), color = color_inst) +
    # apply rescaling
    scale_y_continuous(
      name = "instantaneous",
      sec.axis = sec_axis(~. * rescale, name = "cumulative")
    ) +
    labs(x = "generation time") +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 10))
}

# plot instantaneous and cumulative profile
plot_profile_demo(profile)
```

# Discrete time models

To move to discrete time we need to specify it at the moment of the model generation by adding the option `discr = TRUE`.
Like every custom model, it is compiled at runtime.

```{r}
#| label: load-discrete-model
hhdiscrete <- sarscov2_2021_icofs |>
  new_housepi_model("case-ascertained",
                    discr = TRUE, quiet = TRUE) |>
  add_infectivity_profile(import = "template")
defs <- get_infectivity_profiles(hhdiscrete)
defs
```

A discrete time model discretizes the profile it is given, so the same definition serves both cases.
Note the domain minimum: a discrete time model reads the profile in whole days, and takes the first day of transmission as `min` unless another one is given.
Below we display it as a discretized gamma with those parameters.

```{r}
#| label: plot-discrete-profile
#| fig-alt: >
#|  Discrete instantaneous infectivity profile as a function of the generation day in black.
#|  On a second axis in orange, the corresponding cumulative infectivity profile.
profile <- browse_infectivity_profiles(defs$func, defs$func_args, discr = TRUE)
plot_profile_demo(profile)
```

# Custom infectivity profiles

Imagine we would like to associate a gamma distribution as infectivity profile.
In this case all individuals will share the same profile which depends only on the generation time.
We can provide a custom infectivity profile calling `add_infectivity_profile()` as follows:

```{r}
#| label: add-custom-profile
hhdiscrete <- hhdiscrete |>
  add_infectivity_profile("gamma", shape = 4, scale = 1.3)
defs <- get_infectivity_profiles(hhdiscrete)
defs
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-custom-profile
#| fig-alt: >
#|  Custom discrete instantaneous infectivity profile in black.
#|  On a second axis in orange, the corresponding cumulative infectivity profile.
profile <- browse_infectivity_profiles(defs$func, defs$func_args, discr = TRUE)
plot_profile_demo(profile)
```

If the profiles, distributions or functions currently loaded in housepi are not sufficient to deal with a case study, we provide a mechanism to define custom user functions^[Unfortunately, this requires some programming knowledge in C++.].
We show how to deal with that case in [User functions](user_functions.html).
